body: We encountered the very same issue :+1:

@zoechi, when I visit that plunker - here is the console 

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/7679720/15081396/7099a66c-1388-11e6-97eb-ae84dfb9ecdf.png)
@IEvangelist it's just confirmation. I tried it in Plunker, could reproduce it and thought that I can as well post the Plunker link here in case someone else wants to check it.

Same issue here. From various articles around the web, it seems textContent is preferable to innerText for performance reasons, especially on Webkit-based browsers. I wonder why the latest Angular has forgotten about its validity as a known native property.
A question closely related to this issue... I wonder how we can tell Angular "trust me, there is a property by the name I am using" in the general case, as well as for this specific case.
Yeh, this is a valid bug, I suspect this is due to the fact that we've got a schema now that is "static" and not taken from the browser's runtime properties.
With the amazing pace of commits going in angular/angular nowadays, it would be so nice to include this and other similar small fixes in the flow.
Because I was asked – this is not due to security concern, binding `textContent` should be fine as it is just the inert text of an element (even binding it for `<script>` would be OK). CC @rjamet.

issue.title: feat(SchemaRegistry): add Node.textContent
